criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goals, 4 quantified objectives and rationale linked to Australian benefit. Users and needs explicitly mapped to objectives with literature support. Complete and specific.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS).

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Wk2-Wk10 Gantt with task logic justified by mission order. Explicit contingencies, triggers and responses plus sourced Table 2. Robust and mission-aligned.

evidence.quote: Project work is divided into weeks in the Gantt chart in Figure 1
Week 10 is float as well as editing time

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Correct SSO 600km hand calculations with interpretation of swath vs revisit trade. STK tutorials and scenario started. Clearly on track.

evidence.quote: A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.
Weekly coverage (objective 1) is therefore not guaranteed by one satellite at this altitude and resolution.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear writing, consistent tables and labelled figure. In-text citations match reference list with proper style.

overall: Strong reef-monitoring concept with quantified objectives, justified plan with contingencies, and correct preliminary orbital analysis supporting next design trades.

feedback.summary: You delivered a strong Great Barrier Reef monitoring concept with quantified objectives for AIMS/reef managers, a justified Wk2-Wk10 Gantt with contingencies, and correct 600km SSO analysis in STK. Writing and referencing are clear and professional. Keep this momentum into full trade studies and detailed design.
next_steps: Test alternatives to your single-satellite 600km SSO to close the weekly-coverage gap you identified in Preliminary Progress.
Execute your Figure 1 Gantt in order, using your Week 10 float and contingency triggers if STK or data work slips.
Carry your 4 quantified objectives and AIMS user needs directly into requirements and verification for the full report.

criteria.C1: In Mission Concept & Rationale you set clear reef-colour goals and 4 quantified objectives for AIMS and reef managers, well linked to Australian benefit with literature. You are at Accomplished. To reach full marks, keep that completeness and ensure every objective stays explicitly tied to user needs with references.
criteria.C2: In Project Plan and Figure 1 you justified your Wk2-Wk10 Gantt by mission order and added triggers, responses and Week 10 float with sourced Table 2. You are at Accomplished. To reach full marks, keep showing why the plan fits the reef mission and retain contingency provision.
criteria.C3: In Preliminary Progress and Table 3 you correctly calculated the 600km SSO period, verified it in STK, and interpreted the swath vs revisit limit for weekly coverage. You are at Accomplished and on track. To reach full marks, expand these initial results with brief interpretation guiding next trades.
criteria.C4: Your report uses logical structure, clear writing, consistent tables and labelled Figure 1 Gantt with matching in-text citations and list. You are at Accomplished. To reach full marks, maintain consistent formatting and clear graphical presentation throughout the full report.
